name: Show Marquee
author: Chuck Hergenroeder
description: A sign for your light show on an LED matrix: pages that take turns, each held still for the seconds you choose. A countdown to Christmas, New Year's Day or a date you choose (its number and text each with their own font, size and colour; under a day an HH:MM:SS timer or hours); a weather page with a symbol for the weather (sun, moon, clouds, rain, snow, a storm, fog or wind) beside the temperature and wind; your Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube handles with each site's logo; a show prep page with a QR code viewers scan to get the PulseMesh or Tune2 audio app; your show times; and your own messages, with a colour, a holiday picture and dates for each. Weather comes from the internet weather service Open-Meteo (api.open-meteo.com, which receives this player's location rounded to about 1 km) or from your own WeatherFlow Tempest station on the local network. You choose; weather is off until you turn it on.

privacy.summary: Draws your show's sign pages on a matrix here. With Weather on, it gets weather from Open-Meteo (sending your location, rounded) or hears your Tempest station on your network.

sends.to: http://the FPP player you set as FPP Host (this device by default)
sends.what: requests for the list of overlay models and to turn the chosen model on and off
sends.why: to draw your sign's pages on a matrix attached to that player

sends.what: this player's latitude and longitude, rounded to about 1 km, every 15 minutes
sends.why: for the weather page: temperature, wind and day or night; only with Open-Meteo chosen

collects.what: a weather location you type in instead of FPP's own (latitude and longitude)

systemChanges.what: runs a background program whenever FPP is running, which draws your sign's pages
its background program listens on 127.0.0.1:32330, reachable only from this device; FPP's web server passes requests to it
with Weather on, listens for UDP broadcasts on port 50222 (shared with other listeners) to read a Tempest station; sends nothing

privacy.other: Its API is served through FPP's web server, so anyone who can open this player's FPP pages can change its settings and turn its output on or off, the same as FPP itself. Its FPP commands (countdown on/off, set target) do the same from anything that can run FPP commands, including the scheduler, MQTT and other FPP players. It switches the overlay model you choose on and off and writes pixels into that model's overlay buffer. It writes an activity log (logs/plugin-fpp-showmarquee.log). Uninstalling removes its settings (config/plugin.fpp-showmarquee.json) and a weather location you type in (plugindata/fpp-showmarquee/); a Reinstall keeps them on FPP 10.4 and later.
